C09-M01-L05-F1.title: The custody lifecycle: one record per stage
C09-M01-L05-F1.caption: The eight stages an evidence item passes through, from identification to final disposition, and the record each stage produces.
C09-M01-L05-F1.alt: Top-to-bottom flow of eight rounded boxes: Identify and document in place (photos and scene notes); Collect and label (item number and description); Package and seal (tamper-evident seal number); Issue evidence receipt (signed by collector and witness); Transfer and log each hand-over (both custodians sign); Secure storage (access-logged evidence store); Examine a verified copy (hash checked before and after); Return, retain or dispose (authorised and recorded). A note says every arrow is a hand-over or change of state that must appear in the custody log.
C09-M01-L05-F1.note: Every arrow is a hand-over or change of state that must appear in the custody log.

C09-M01-L05-F2.title: Reading a custody log: links that hold and links that break
C09-M01-L05-F2.caption: Six entries from the fictional custody log for laptop KF-031-E01, with two defects a reviewer must raise.
C09-M01-L05-F2.alt: Table with columns #, Date, time (IST), Released by, Received by, and Purpose and seal. Row 1, green: 14 Mar 10:42, on site desk 3B, A. Rao, collected with seal KS-4471. Row 2, green: 14 Mar 17:05, A. Rao, P. Iyer at the store, lodged with KS-4471 intact. Row 3, green: 16 Mar 09:30, P. Iyer, S. Menon, imaging, resealed KS-4490. Row 4, red: 16 Mar 16:15, S. Menon, P. Iyer, returned with seal recorded as KS-4471, contradicting row 3. Row 5, slate: 18 Mar 14:00, P. Iyer, S. Menon, re-check of serial. Row 6, red: 23 Mar 11:10, J. Das, P. Iyer, returned with unexplained seal KS-4502 and no transfer from S. Menon to J. Das. A note says entries 4 and 6 must be raised and neither is fixed by editing the log afterwards.
C09-M01-L05-F2.note: Entries 4 and 6 must be raised in writing; neither is fixed by editing the log afterwards.
